question: What doctrinal identity is assigned to the soul when it is identified as the Haṃsa and as power joined to an individual, while being declared more supreme than others?
premises: It is more supreme than what is ordinarily called soul.
The relative clause identifies a specific one as that supreme entity.
That entity is designated the Haṃsa and is power joined to an individual.
inference: The supreme soul is identified technically as the Haṃsa, understood as power conjoined with the individual.
uncertainties: The precise relation between śakti and pudgala is not unpacked in this verse.
plain_english: He is the soul, more supreme. Indeed, he who is that is the Haṃsa, power joined to an individual.
